Unscented Kalman filter localization

Source: R/ukf-slam.R
robot_ukf.Rd

A drop-in alternative to robot_ekf() that propagates the planar pose with the unscented transform instead of Jacobians. The covariance lives in the local tangent chart of the pose: the heading deviation is an unwrapped angle, so a broad heading uncertainty is never folded back by wrapping. ukf_predict() augments the state with the control noise, draws \(2(3 + 2) + 1\) sigma points, moves each through unicycle_step() with its noisy control and keeps its heading change unwrapped. ukf_update() fuses range-bearing measurements of known landmarks one at a time; predicted bearings are averaged as wrapped differences from the bearing of the central sigma point, so signed weights are handled exactly, and the state deviations used for the cross covariance are the sigma deviations themselves, consistent with cov.

Usage

robot_ukf(mean, cov, landmarks, Q, R, alpha = 1, beta = 2, kappa = 0)

ukf_predict(filter, control, dt)

ukf_update(filter, measurements)

Arguments

mean

Initial pose estimate.

cov

Initial 3 by 3 covariance.

landmarks

Matrix of landmark positions with row names as ids.

Q

Control noise covariance (2 by 2).

R

Measurement noise covariance (2 by 2).

alpha, beta, kappa

Unscented transform parameters.

filter

A robot_ukf.

control

c(v, omega).

dt

Duration (s).

measurements

A data frame as returned by landmark_measurements().

Value

A robot_ukf. ukf_update() also records the normalized innovation squared in nis.

Details

The default scaling alpha = 1, beta = 2, kappa = 0 makes every weight nonnegative, which keeps every covariance positive semidefinite. Other scalings (for example a small alpha) give a negative central weight; a result that is then indefinite stops with an error instead of being returned. alpha must be positive and kappa > -3, so that the transform is defined for both the 3 dimensional state and the 5 dimensional augmented state.

Examples

L <- rbind(a = c(2, 0), b = c(0, 2))
f <- robot_ukf(c(0, 0, 0), diag(0.1, 3), L, Q = diag(c(0.01, 0.01)),
               R = diag(c(0.01, 0.001)))
f <- ukf_predict(f, c(1, 0), 0.1)
f <- ukf_update(f, landmark_measurements(c(0.1, 0, 0), L))
f$mean
#>           x           y       theta 
#>  0.11239768 -0.00626806  0.00510093
